ca_renaissance_crag.blurb: Renaissance Crag is a steep, overhanging cliff in Rattlesnake Canyon above Santa Barbara, at roughly 2,000 feet. It has nine routes, five sport and four trad, spanning 5.8 to 5.13. The upper end is well stocked, with two sport lines at 5.13 and one at 5.12, while the trad routes mostly fall between 5.8 and 5.11. The rock is hard and can be abrasive. The wall stays shaded and rarely draws a crowd. It is the first crag you meet on the right when hiking up the canyon, with the Alchemist cliffs across the creek.
ca_renaissance_crag.parking_note: Leave the car at the Rattlesnake Canyon trailhead and hike up the canyon trail.

ca_meteorite_the.blurb: The Meteorite is a single isolated boulder on the north bank of the South Yuba River at Edward's Crossing, near Nevada City. It has nine problems, from the easiest warm-ups at about V-easy up to V5 and harder, with most of them between V0 and V3 and two in the V5 range. Because it sits on its own, all the problems are gathered around one block. Reaching it takes a short walk along the river from the Edward's Crossing bridge.

ca_futthead_rock.blurb: Futthead Rock is a small crag in the Magic Mountain Area of Joshua Tree National Park, in the Pinto Basin near the 29 Palms entrance, at about 3,100 feet. It has nine routes: seven sport, one trad and one top rope. Most are moderate, with three at 5.5, a few from 5.7 to 5.9, and a single 5.10. The rock is decent and the routes are a mix of older and newer lines. Getting there is a cross-country hike that follows cairns, with Elf's Hat serving as the landmark to keep in view, so it suits a party happy to route-find.

ca_idyllwild_dome.blurb: Idyllwild Dome is a small formation in the Echo Rock Area of central Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,300 feet, set back behind the Echo Cove cliffs. It has nine routes, mostly trad (six), plus two sport and one top rope. Grades run from 5.4 up to 5.10, with most lines at 5.9 and 5.10 and just a couple of easy ones. Climbs are spread over several sides of the dome, many of them on slab. Reaching the base means about 15 minutes of walking across open desert from a pullout.

ca_dilbert_dome.blurb: Dilbert Dome is a small outcrop facing northwest, in the Comic Book Area of central Joshua Tree National Park. It is built in two tiers: the lower one is steep and holds a few crack climbs, while the upper one is slabby and knobby. There are nine routes, seven trad, one sport and one top rope, from 5.3 up to low 5.11, with a good share in the moderate range. The base is about five minutes on foot from the roadside pullouts.
